chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all together, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Al-Walid ibn Sabih, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Regarding the wergild (blood money) of the Saluqi dog, it is forty dirhams. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) ordered that it be paid to the Clan of Juzayma.

key_terms.الْكَلْبِ السَّلُوقِيِّ: The Saluqi dog, a specific breed of hunting dog
key_terms.دِيَة: Wergild or blood money, financial compensation for injury or death

ai.seo_question: What is the blood money (diyah) for a Saluqi dog in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi specifies the blood money (diyah) for a Saluqi dog as forty dirhams, a ruling attributed directly to the Prophet Muhammad and designated for the Banu Juzayma clan. It highlights the Shia tradition of recognizing specific animal valuations within Islamic jurisprudence, distinguishing the Saluqi (a hunting breed) from other livestock in terms of compensation. The attribution to the Prophet underscores the continuity of prophetic authority in determining financial liabilities for non-human creatures.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazal Bin Shazaan, both together, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ibrahim Bin Abdul Hameed, from Al Waleed Bin Sabeeh, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>
having said regarding wergild of the greyhound dog being forty Dirhams. Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> ordered it to be paid to the Clan of Juzayma’.
